summary: Rewrite the two lock tests in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/suggestions_test.go around one helper, suggestionsBehindLock: it sets srv.suggestionTimeout = lockedSuggestionAllowance (5 s) on a directServer, takes the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock in a held transaction, runs computeAndPersistSuggestions in a goroutine, polls pg_locks through the holder transaction for a backend blocked by it (failing at once if the answer arrives first), then receives the answer with no timer; each test asserts non-nil with Missing set. Add the zero-Deps sentence at register and name every setter in the suggestionTimeout comment (server.go), and a dated INFRA-260 note on the INFRA-56 knob solution doc's 'Still open' paragraph.
decisions: Allowance 5 s: bounds only time-to-lock (test 2's first statement is the locked one; test 1 runs one table-free numnode round trip first); 737 ms worst on record for a whole filing under load; sjawhar/legion#2158 ran asks-locked at 5 s 5 of 5. Costs ~+9 s per package run.
No timer on the answer and no deadline on the waiter poll (AC1 forbids a fixed elapsed bound): a regression waits behind the lock until go test -timeout panics, naming the test.

Waiter tied to the test's lock: select count(*) from pg_locks where not granted and pg_backend_pid() = any(pg_blocking_pids(pid)), queried through the holder transaction (storetest.WaitForLockWaiters' query); no SQL-text pin; checked only before the answer arrives.
Test 1 drops the answered-ask seeding (suggestions_test.go:266-274): with asks locked the fused search waits first and the decision lookup is unreachable (sjawhar/legion#2158).
Assert Missing set, never its text; no CHANGELOG/README change (nothing a user meets changes).

acceptance.criterion: Neither test asserts elapsed wall-clock time against a fixed bound; each sets suggestionTimeout on its own server and asserts a non-nil result with Missing set, reached while its query waits behind the lock.

findings.finding: AC2's 'package's suite' is ambiguous (whole package vs -run subset); a whole-package copy took 851 s alone so three concurrent copies exceed go test's default 10 min; skip vs pass needs -v or -json.
findings.answer: Read as the whole internal/dispatch/api package; command uses -count=1 -timeout 240m -json, outputs under $TMPDIR/infra260/copyN.json, and a jq check per copy that prints both test names with pass and no skip.

findings.finding: Whether a liveness guard counts as a forbidden fixed bound is open; with no timer a regression hangs until the package -timeout panic.
findings.answer: Decision 2: no timer on the answer or on the waiter poll, matching AC1 literally; a regression costs a -timeout panic naming the test. Recorded as a risk.

findings.finding: lockWaiters counts any lock waiter in the database, not the call's query behind the test's lock.
findings.answer: Decision 3: count pg_locks waiters whose pg_blocking_pids include the holder transaction's backend, queried through the holder transaction; no SQL-text pattern.

findings.finding: Test 1's comment claims the decision lookup is bounded; with asks locked the search blocks first, so the answered-ask seeding is dead and both comments/messages describe a stopwatch.
findings.answer: Decisions 5-7: test 1's comment says it proves the search under the allowance and that the decision lookup is unreachable under this lock; seeding dropped; failure messages name no duration.

findings.finding: server.go suggestionTimeout comment names only newFailingAdviceHandler; the INFRA-56 solution doc calls these tests 'Still open'.
findings.answer: Decisions 9-10: name every setter; append a dated Note 2026-10-25 (INFRA-260) to that paragraph.

findings.finding: The generous allowance is still a bound on time-to-lock and each test spends it in full; mutation controls are per test.
findings.answer: Decision 1 states 5 s, its margin over 737 ms on record and its ~+9 s cost; controls b and c each map to the one test they must break.

findings.finding: The register sentence covers dialing but not dereferencing the nil Store, which newDeliveryHub would do.
findings.answer: Decision 8: the sentence also says it must not read the nil Store; it must contain 'zero Deps', 'cheap' and 'must not dial'.

findings.finding: pgx may leave the backend queued after the client returns on a deadline.
findings.answer: Decision 3: the helper checks for a waiter only before the answer arrives and never waits for it to clear.

findings.finding: Spec title says 'measured as too tight' while the body says the margin is inferred; nproc and compiler availability must be checked at run time.
findings.answer: The title is the spec owner's; it changes no work. The plan records -race as CI's (no C compiler in the pod, as INFRA-56 found) and has the implementer check the port and rig at run time.

risks: A machine that cannot queue one statement within 5 s fails AC1 with the helper's message.
A regression in the bounded context costs a package -timeout panic, not a named failure.
AC2's three whole-package copies take tens of minutes and need max_connections raised.
